record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex have vanishing higher homotopy groups, and therefore is every such subcomplex itself aspherical?

evidence.quote: whether a subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex need also have vanishing higher homotopy groups

artifact.self_contained_problem: A connected CW complex $L$ of dimension at most $2$ is called aspherical if its higher homotopy groups vanish, equivalently if $\pi_2(L)=0$ (so that its universal cover is contractible). Question: Is it true that for every aspherical $2$-dimensional CW complex $L$ and every connected subcomplex $K \subseteq L$, one has $\pi_n(K)=0$ for all $n\geq 2$ (so that $K$ is itself aspherical)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Whitehead asphericity conjecture, posed in 1941, remains a long-standing open problem in low-dimensional topology and combinatorial group theory. Recent preprints (e.g., a 2023/2024 arXiv preprint by Kawauchi using ribbon sphere-links) claim a resolution but have not gained acceptance in the mathematical community. Wikipedia and survey sources continue to list the conjecture as open.

status_evidence.title: Whitehead conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Whitehead conjecture is a long-standing open problem in algebraic topology, formulated by J. H. C. Whitehead in 1941.

status_evidence.title: Whitehead aspherical conjecture via ribbon sphere-link (arXiv:2303.04368)
status_evidence.snippet: Claimed proof of the Whitehead aspherical conjecture via ribbon sphere-link arguments.
status_evidence.claim: A recent proof attempt exists but has not been broadly accepted.
